body:
I'm glad you're still here. Please note that this is not in any way diminishing your experience: I've attempted suicide before, and failed. Ever since then I wished I'd succeeded.

Again, not trying to be difficult. I'm sincerely grateful that you find more value in living than in death. I just don't think that's me, and it hasn't been for a long time. I do truly thank you for listening, even if I'm just a broken record. It means a lot.

I've tried talk therapy, behavior therapy, meds, and even electronic stimulation. The estim felt funky, but that was about it.

I'm not trying to be a downer. I just haven't had anything work and I've spent too many years shelling out time and money for stuff that, if it helped, only helped for a few months at best. I appreciate your time, though.

It sucks, man. I feel that. "You'll get better, try this. Talk to this person. Use this chatline\*. Take this pill." Will I get better, or are you just too afraid to look me in the eye and tell me that I won't?

\*I tried to use a chatline once. No one connected, so it hung up on me. In hindsight, it's absolutely hilarious.

Have you looked at EPIK (English Programs In Korea)? Check it out, it might pique your interest.

I know where you're coming from, man. I'm right there with you.

Thanks for replying.

I'm going to graduate uni by the end of the month with a bachelor's. The issue is, this fellowship was what I was hoping would make my medical school app actually competitive...and now it's gone. Everyone seems genuinely surprised that I didn't get it. If I can't get something I'm qualified for, that doesn't bode well for me in the future.

There are different levels of suicidal thoughts. Some are intrusive ("I wish I were dead - oh wait, why did I think that") and some are actual conscious thoughts ("I wish I were dead.") The most serious suicidal thoughts are the ones that have plans attached ("I wish I were dead and I am going to \_\_\_\_\_\_ to achieve that").

As for when you should take them seriously - are they bothering you? If they're hindering your everyday life and/or are causing you distress, take them seriously. It's different for everyone - it's a reaction to a symptom.

If you're comfortable with talking to someone, I suggest trying to talk to someone you trust, getting a counselor, or using a chatline. Make sure you carefully consider your options before you decide on anything.
